entities.summary: Yang Yu (1364–1444), better known by his courtesy name as Yang Shiqi, was a Chinese scholar-official during the Ming dynasty. He served as grand secretary during the reigns of emperors Yongle, Hongxi, Xuande, and Yingzong from 1402 until his death, with a brief hiatus in 1414. In 1424, he became the leader of the corps of grand secretaries, effectively holding the position of informal head of the Chinese government.
